slides.title: The Biggest Year 2 Risk Is Complacency
slides.content: Students already know the systems. The risk is: Assuming problems are fine. Not reporting concerns. Becoming casual about safety. Thinking support is no longer needed. "Don't fumble the last lap."

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'The Biggest Year 2 Risk Is Complacency'? Select all that apply.
options: Thinking support is no longer needed
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on The Biggest Year 2 Risk Is Complacency.

slides.title: Year 2 Pressures Are Different
slides.content: Common Year 2 pressures include: Final Major Projects. UCAS and progression applications. Industry placements. Financial pressures. Relationships. Freelance work. These pressures can increase safeguarding risks.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Year 2 Pressures Are Different'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Year 2 Pressures Are Different.

slides.title: Safeguarding Still Matters
slides.content: Nothing has changed about: Access to safeguarding support. Access to wellbeing services. Reporting routes. Staff responsibilities. Many Year 2 students need support but use it less often.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Safeguarding Still Matters'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Safeguarding Still Matters.

slides.title: Peer Responsibility Becomes More Important
slides.content: By Year 2: You know your peers. You recognise changes in behaviour. You spot concerns earlier. That knowledge is a responsibility. If someone appears to be struggling, encourage them to seek support or raise a concern.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Peer Responsibility Becomes More Important'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Peer Responsibility Becomes More Important.

slides.title: New Online Risks
slides.content: Year 2 brings: Job scams. Fake freelance opportunities. Fake agency offers. Exploitative contracts. Greater public visibility through portfolios. Professional identity becomes more important.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'New Online Risks'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on New Online Risks.

slides.title: AI Rules Matter More
slides.content: Year 2 assessed work receives greater scrutiny. Examples include: Final Major Projects. Occupational Specialism Projects. Major coursework. Externally moderated assessments. Students must understand and follow AI declaration requirements.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'AI Rules Matter More'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on AI Rules Matter More.

slides.title: Consent Matters
slides.content: A key Year 2 reminder: Always obtain proper consent when: Filming people. Photographing people. Sharing media. Familiarity is not permission. Friends still deserve consent.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Consent Matters'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Consent Matters.

slides.title: Reporting Concerns Is Still Essential
slides.content: Many Year 2 students avoid reporting concerns because they think they should manage independently. This is a mistake. The correct action is still: Tell someone early. Seek support. Use safeguarding and wellbeing routes.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Reporting Concerns Is Still Essential'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Reporting Concerns Is Still Essential.

slides.title: Professional Reputation Matters
slides.content: Your digital footprint now affects: University applications. Placement opportunities. Employment prospects. Professional reputation. Your online presence is part of your professional identity.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Professional Reputation Matters'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Professional Reputation Matters.

slides.title: Quick Revision Summary
slides.content: Key points to remember: Avoid complacency Manage increased pressures appropriately Look out for peers Protect your professional reputation Follow stricter AI requirements Continue reporting concerns and seeking support when needed. ,

exercise.prompt: Which of these points are in the quick revision summary? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: These points are summarised in the Quick Revision Summary.
